requiredFindings.title: Close the package/subpath grammar and canonical path rules
requiredFindings.finding: The new resolution law refers to the npm package-name grammar without selecting a closed grammar, and defines a subpath only as the remainder after the name. It does not decide empty segments, dot/dot-dot segments, backslashes, trailing separators or encoded separators, nor state how a candidate spelling becomes the canonical project-relative node identity. The clause any other form that names a filesystem path is also not a closed discriminator from package forms. Inputs such as pkg/../base, pkg//base and pkg\base therefore lack a stated malformed/unresolved/normalized result. Canonical node identity matters for repeated edges, cycles and the 32-node limit, not just filesystem opening.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Specify or pin the exact name grammar, close the subpath/path-form grammar, state normalization and root-containment timing, and define canonical graph node identity before deduplication/cycle/bound checks. Add explicit disposition controls for these ambiguous forms while preserving the selected candidate order.

requiredFindings.title: Route the new public detail to a remedy under its own public key
requiredFindings.finding: Item 14a assigns public DomainDetailCode native.typescript-config-unresolved but says its remedy comes through B-S9's CONFIG.INVALID route. B-S9 explicitly states that PUBLIC_ROUTE_REMEDIES is keyed by public detail, and that keys whose public detail is not CONFIG.INVALID are outside that string even if their D9 code is CONFIG.INVALID. Thus the selected D9 code does not select that remedy entry. S10 repeats the ambiguous route and does not explicitly require the new public-key remedy/carrier mapping.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Keep D9 CONFIG.INVALID distinct from the public detail key. Require S10 to register the remedy/route under native.typescript-config-unresolved in the appropriate successor model/product carrier, with one remedy true for all four internal aliases; alternatively deliberately reuse the existing public CONFIG.INVALID detail and revise the new-record decision. State how each alias reaches a complete public termination and remedy.
